compiled_state.description:
# Bounded self-cleaning live-Jira-Cloud coordinator lifecycle lane + search-index-lag hardening

## Problem
The epic's Live-External AC requires the RP-03 create-coordinator's create / binding-lifecycle /
commit-unknown / fuse exercised against **live Jira Cloud**. The only Cloud lane today is read-only AND
gated off (`vars.AWS_S3_REHEARSAL_ROLE_ARN` unset) — SKIPPED even in green runs — so **no run has exercised
live-Cloud mutation**. Separately, `bridge check-access`'s `STEP_JQL_SEARCH` flakes on live REB: its wait
is a FIXED 6x5s (no backoff), shorter than Jira Cloud's Lucene-index lag — the write lands (the by-key read
right after passes), only SEARCH visibility lags.

## §1 — Harden the search-index wait (`access_check.py`)
Replace the fixed 6x5s loop with an env-tunable exponential-backoff budget:
- `JIRA_PROBE_JQL_RETRIES` (default 10; was 6), `JIRA_PROBE_JQL_SLEEP` base (default 3; was 5),
  `JIRA_PROBE_JQL_SLEEP_MAX` cap (default 30).- Sleep before retry k (k over 0..RETRIES-2) is `min(base*2**k, cap)` → defaults `[3,6,12,24,30,30,30,30,30]`
  = 195s worst case (old ~25s budget timed out). Follows the capped-exponential shape used by the acli retry
  floor (`_errors.MAX_BACKOFF_S`) but as a positive-result visibility poll. The `sleep_fn` seam is kept
  (unit-testable without real sleeping); this poll helper is reused by §2's commit-unknown wait.

## §2 — Live-Cloud coordinator lifecycle module (bounded, self-cleaning)
NEW `tests/external/live_jira_cloud_mutation/test_cloud_coordinator_lifecycle.py` (+ `conftest.py`). Against
live REB it drives the epic's CREATE route `coordinate_full_create` for a plan of EXACTLY ONE throwaway
ticket, then exercises the fuse via a bounded follow-up mutation:
- **Write-bounding (shared-prod safety).** No full `bridge sync`, no legacy `--filter-local-ids`; acts only
  on the ONE plan handed to it (one create) — no enumeration, no write-back. The only possible Jira
  mutations are the throwaway issue's create, its containment label/property, and its delete.
- **create + binding-lifecycle.** Physical create via the live Cloud client; record_key/attach_label/
  set_property/confirm bind+contain it; asserts a confirmed containment (`dependents_released`) with `jira`
  channel + `jira-` provenance.
- **commit-unknown recovery.** A second call injects an ambiguous create signal so `_resolve_ambiguous`
  re-observes ONCE and ADOPTS the existing issue (no duplicate); its `observe` first waits on the dedup
  label search (reusing §1's helper) so adoption is attributable to dedup, not lag.
- **fuse.** A bounded non-create mutation on the bound throwaway key is driven through
  `batch_dispatch.coordinate_and_fuse([mutation_plan], execute=...)`; asserts the returned `CutoverReport`
  (tallies + fuse_decisions + degraded) reflects that op.
- **teardown (always).** ONE env label `${REBAR_PROBE_RUN_LABEL}` stamped on the issue; deletes by key in a
  `finally`, then sweeps any issue carrying THAT label (the value §3's sweep keys on) — scoped to this run.
- Gated by `_live_jira_ready()` + `REBAR_RUN_EXTERNAL=1` + Cloud creds; enrols in the all-skip canary.
## §3 — Workflow lane
Add `jira-cloud-mutation-probe` to `.github/workflows/external-integration.yml` (`workflow_dispatch` +
weekly cron): export `REBAR_PROBE_RUN_LABEL=rebar-id:cloudprobe-${{ github.run_id }}` + REB Cloud env from
secrets, run `bridge check-access` (preflight) THEN the module, and on BOTH failure AND cancel run an
always-run teardown sweeping `${REBAR_PROBE_RUN_LABEL}` via acli (`acli jira workitem search --jql
"labels = ..." --json` then `acli jira workitem delete --key <KEY> --yes` per hit; `--yes` REQUIRED per acli.py bug-3256, else the non-TTY sweep blocks on stdin). Same label the module stamps, scoping the sweep to the run. **Anti-masquerade:** NO credential-based job-level `if:` gate — the job always runs on dispatch/cron with `REBAR_RUN_EXTERNAL=1`, so absent creds don't render the lane neutral; its tests all-skip and `tests/external/conftest.py`'s fail-on-all-skip canary flips the session RED (a skipped Cloud lane FAILS).

## §4 — Workflow-structure unit test
`tests/unit/test_external_integration_cloud_mutation_workflow.py` (modelled on
`test_jira_dc_capability_map_workflow.py`) proves the lane exists, exports `REBAR_PROBE_RUN_LABEL` from the
run id, runs check-access + the module, and has an always-run teardown with `--yes` keyed on that label.
## §5 — Docs
Update `tests/external/live_jira_cloud_s3/README.md`: the read-only rule is that suite's choice; the new
lane is bounded, self-cleaning, prod-safe.

## Prerequisites (operational)
The Cloud lane needs live REB Cloud credentials as repo config — `JIRA_URL` and `JIRA_USER` as repository
**variables** and `JIRA_API_TOKEN` as a repository **secret** (the exact names the workflow's env block and
`tests/external/live_jira_cloud_mutation/_cloud_mutation_support._CLOUD_CRED_VARS` consume). The operator
provisions/confirms them BEFORE the GREEN-run AC is evaluated. Missing creds cannot masquerade as success:
the module enrols in the all-skip canary, so a skipped Cloud lane FAILS.

## Consumers to update (enumerated)
- `tests/scripts/bridge/test_jira_capability_probe.py` (asserts `call_count == 6`, `delays == [5,5,5,5,5]`)
  updated in the SAME change to the new 10-attempt `delays == [3,6,12,24,30,30,30,30,30]` plus an
  env-override case recomputing from overridden base/cap/retries.

## Surface-parity census
- CLI (`bridge check-access`): in scope — JQL backoff exercised through it.
- library (`run_access_check`; `coordinate_full_create`+`PassFuse`): in scope — unit tests drive the
  backoff; the live module drives the create route + fuse.
- automated caller (lane / live module): in scope — E2E oracle is the live run.
- MCP/API: out of scope (no MCP tool). dual-direction: outbound create only in a one-plan call, no mirror.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `access_check.py` JQL wait is env-tunable exponential backoff (defaults 10 / 3 / 30 → sleeps
  `[3,6,12,24,30,...]`); `sleep_fn` seam preserved; write-landing still confirmed by the by-key read.
  Evidenced by new unit tests asserting the schedule and env-override recomputation.
- [x] `tests/scripts/bridge/test_jira_capability_probe.py` updated to the new schedule/defaults and passes.
- [x] The live-Cloud module drives `coordinate_full_create` for ONE throwaway plan (create/binding +
  commit-unknown-after-visibility-wait + fuse), asserts known_key is the throwaway key and no other, and
  ALWAYS deletes (finally + `${REBAR_PROBE_RUN_LABEL}` sweep). Enrols in the all-skip canary.
- [x] The `jira-cloud-mutation-probe` lane exports `REBAR_PROBE_RUN_LABEL`, runs check-access + module, and
  has an always-run `acli jira workitem delete --key <KEY> --yes` teardown keyed on that label. Per §4.
- [x] [operator-attested] With Cloud secrets provisioned (see Prerequisites), a dispatched Live External Integration run shows
  provenance: environment=live Jira Cloud + live Jira Data Center (GitHub Actions external-integration.yml); principal=CI external-integration service credentials (REBAR_PROBE); privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — run 33137402410 exercised the new Cloud-mutation lane and the DC harness lane, both GREEN; run URL commented on the epic.
  the new Cloud-mutation lane GREEN and the DC lane GREEN. Evidenced by the run URL commented on the epic.
- [x] `tests/external/live_jira_cloud_s3/README.md` documents the read-only rule as suite-scoped and the
  new bounded self-cleaning mutating lane.
- [x] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` green.

## Verify commands
- `make test PYTEST_ARGS="tests/scripts/bridge/test_jira_capability_probe.py tests/unit/test_external_integration_cloud_mutation_workflow.py"` and `make lint`

## Portability
CI-agnostic: backoff is library behavior; the lane surfaces an op-linked probe (check-access + a
pytest module) that runs locally with the same env — nothing gated on one CI system.
